Apple___Apple_scab.description: A common fungal disease that causes dark, scabby spots on leaves and fruit, reducing fruit quality.
Apple___Apple_scab.recommended_action: Remove fallen leaves, prune infected branches, and apply fungicides like Captan or Mancozeb early in the season.

Apple___Black_rot.description: A fungal disease that causes circular brown spots on leaves and black, shriveled fruit known as mummies.
Apple___Black_rot.recommended_action: Prune and destroy infected limbs and fruit. Apply copper-based fungicide before bloom.

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.description: Yellow-orange leaf spots and deformed fruits, caused by a fungus that cycles between apple and cedar trees.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.recommended_action: Remove nearby cedar hosts if possible and apply fungicides containing Myclobutanil at pink bud stage.

Apple___healthy.description: The apple tree appears normal with clean leaves and unblemished fruits.
Apple___healthy.recommended_action: Continue regular pruning and watering. Monitor for early signs of disease.

Blueberry___healthy.description: The blueberry plant shows green foliage and healthy fruit with no visible disease.
Blueberry___healthy.recommended_action: Maintain soil acidity and avoid waterlogging to prevent root diseases.

Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.description: White, powdery coating forms on leaves, shoots, and fruit, slowing growth and reducing yield.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.recommended_action: Prune overcrowded branches, improve airflow, and apply sulfur-based fungicides.

Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.description: Cherry plant shows shiny green leaves and clean fruit without mold or spots.
Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.recommended_action: Maintain good pruning and watering practices to avoid fungal diseases.

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.description: Gray to tan rectangular lesions appear on leaves, reducing photosynthesis and yield.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.recommended_action: Plant resistant hybrids, rotate crops, and apply fungicide like Azoxystrobin if disease spreads.

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.description: Reddish-brown pustules appear on leaves, caused by the Puccinia sorghi fungus.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.recommended_action: Use resistant corn hybrids and spray fungicides such as Trifloxystrobin when rust is severe.

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.description: Large, grayish-brown lesions appear on leaves, reducing the plant’s ability to produce energy.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.recommended_action: Rotate crops, plant resistant varieties, and use fungicides at tasseling if conditions are favorable.

Corn_(maize)___healthy.description: The corn plant is free of rusts and leaf blights, showing strong and even leaf coloration.
Corn_(maize)___healthy.recommended_action: Maintain good field hygiene and balanced fertilization to prevent disease outbreaks.

Grape___Black_rot.description: Fungal disease causing brown leaf spots and black shriveled fruit, especially in humid conditions.
Grape___Black_rot.recommended_action: Remove infected debris and apply fungicides such as Mancozeb or Captan before bloom.

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).description: Causes leaf striping, fruit spots, and internal wood decay, leading to vine dieback.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).recommended_action: Prune infected wood, avoid injuries during pruning, and maintain proper irrigation to reduce stress.

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.description: Small angular spots on leaves that coalesce and cause leaf drop, reducing yield.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.recommended_action: Remove fallen leaves, improve air circulation, and apply fungicides containing copper or sulfur.

Grape___healthy.description: The grapevine shows lush green leaves and firm, disease-free grapes.
Grape___healthy.recommended_action: Ensure proper pruning, spacing, and watering to keep vines strong and disease-free.

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).description: A serious bacterial infection that causes yellow shoots, misshapen fruit, and tree death.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).recommended_action: Remove infected trees to prevent spread and control psyllid vectors using approved insecticides.

Peach___Bacterial_spot.description: Dark, sunken spots appear on leaves and fruit, leading to premature leaf drop and blemished peaches.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.recommended_action: Plant resistant cultivars, prune infected twigs, and apply copper-based bactericides.

Peach___healthy.description: The peach tree shows smooth leaves and clean fruits with no visible spots.
Peach___healthy.recommended_action: Prune regularly to maintain airflow and prevent bacterial buildup.

Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.description: Small, water-soaked lesions appear on leaves and fruit, turning brown and scabby over time.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.recommended_action: Use disease-free seeds, avoid overhead watering, and spray copper-based fungicides.

Pepper,_bell___healthy.description: Bell pepper plants have firm green leaves and shiny fruit without blemishes.
Pepper,_bell___healthy.recommended_action: Keep plants well-spaced and watered to prevent stress-related infections.

Potato___Early_blight.description: Dark, circular spots with concentric rings appear on lower leaves, leading to leaf drop.
Potato___Early_blight.recommended_action: Remove affected leaves and apply fungicides like Mancozeb or Chlorothalonil.

Potato___Late_blight.description: Causes brown patches and water-soaked lesions on leaves and stems, leading to rapid decay.
Potato___Late_blight.recommended_action: Destroy infected plants, avoid overhead watering, and spray fungicides like Metalaxyl.

Potato___healthy.description: The potato plant has dark green foliage and firm tubers with no visible blight.
Potato___healthy.recommended_action: Use certified seeds and rotate crops to reduce soil-borne pathogens.

Raspberry___healthy.description: The raspberry bush is vigorous and shows no signs of leaf spot or canker.
Raspberry___healthy.recommended_action: Maintain good pruning and watering habits to prevent fungal growth.

Soybean___healthy.description: Soybean plants appear uniform and green with no signs of leaf blight or rust.
Soybean___healthy.recommended_action: Ensure crop rotation and good drainage to prevent soil-borne diseases.

Squash___Powdery_mildew.description: White, powdery spots appear on leaves, leading to yellowing and curling.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.recommended_action: Provide good air circulation, avoid excess nitrogen, and spray sulfur or neem oil-based fungicides.

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.description: Small purple spots merge into brown patches, drying leaf edges and reducing yield.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.recommended_action: Remove old leaves, avoid overhead irrigation, and apply copper-based sprays if needed.

Strawberry___healthy.description: Strawberry plants have bright green leaves and firm red fruits without any discoloration.
Strawberry___healthy.recommended_action: Water regularly and mulch around the base to retain moisture and prevent fungal spores.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.description: Small water-soaked spots appear on leaves and fruit, later turning brown and scabby.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.recommended_action: Avoid overhead watering and apply copper-based bactericides. Remove infected plants if severe.

Tomato___Early_blight.description: Dark brown spots with concentric rings appear on lower leaves, causing premature defoliation.
Tomato___Early_blight.recommended_action: Use crop rotation, remove old plant debris, and spray fungicides like Chlorothalonil.

Tomato___Late_blight.description: Irregular gray-green patches appear on leaves that quickly turn brown and rot.
Tomato___Late_blight.recommended_action: Destroy affected plants, avoid water on leaves, and use Metalaxyl-based fungicides.

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.description: Yellow patches appear on upper leaf surfaces, with gray mold on the underside.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.recommended_action: Increase air circulation, reduce humidity, and spray fungicides like Chlorothalonil.

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.description: Small, circular gray spots with dark borders appear on lower leaves, causing leaf drop.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.recommended_action: Remove infected leaves and apply fungicides containing Mancozeb or Copper Hydroxide.

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.description: Tiny spider mites cause yellow speckling on leaves and fine webbing underneath.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.recommended_action: Spray insecticidal soap or neem oil. Increase humidity to reduce mite population.

Tomato___Target_Spot.description: Circular spots with concentric rings appear on leaves, resembling a target pattern.
Tomato___Target_Spot.recommended_action: Remove infected leaves and apply fungicides containing Chlorothalonil or Mancozeb.

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.description: Viral infection causing upward curling leaves and stunted growth.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.recommended_action: Control whitefly vectors and remove infected plants immediately.

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.description: Leaves develop light and dark green mottled patterns, and fruit may be distorted.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.recommended_action: Avoid handling healthy plants after touching infected ones. Disinfect tools regularly.

Tomato___healthy.description: Tomato plants have bright green leaves and firm, red fruits without spots or mold.
Tomato___healthy.recommended_action: Provide adequate spacing and regular watering to promote strong, healthy growth.
